summary: Refuse asynchronous config admission when the native lock entry is a foreign filesystem object.

patterns: Config callbacks are synchronous and operate through native contained directories.
constraints: Only successful native lock acquisition may admit a callback. Foreign entries are never ownership grants.
Preserve callback failures and native release. Do not delete or repair foreign objects.
Preserve the public entry points and native ownership protocol. Do not replace file operations with stubs.

milestones.goal: Refuse asynchronous config admission when the native lock entry is a foreign filesystem object.

tasks.description: Refuse asynchronous config admission when the native lock entry is a foreign filesystem object.
test_scenarios: A symbolic link at the lock name rejects before invoking the callback and leaves the link and its target unchanged.
A directory at the lock name rejects before invoking the callback and preserves its contents.
An admitted callback failure is propagated exactly once, and its native lock is released.

milestones.qualitative_verification: Confirm the implementation retains descriptor-bound native operations.

success_criteria: A symbolic link at the lock name rejects before invoking the callback and leaves the link and its target unchanged.
A directory at the lock name rejects before invoking the callback and preserves its contents.
An admitted callback failure is propagated exactly once, and its native lock is released.

directives.text: Only successful native lock acquisition may admit a callback. Foreign entries are never ownership grants.
directives.completion_check: Native acceptance scenarios pass without weakening ownership.
